priority.P0: Do now. User-visible breakage, silent data loss, or a security control that fails with low preconditions. Small, low-risk fixes.
priority.P1: Next. Security issues that need preconditions, data-integrity gaps, or things that block agents from working safely.
priority.P2: Planned. Hardening, performance, operational risk, documentation that misleads.
priority.P3: Backlog. Hygiene and design debt with low current impact.

confidence.verified-runtime: Reproduced against a running instance (PHP 8.4.21 + PostgreSQL 16.13, migrations from this commit).
confidence.verified-static: Established by reading the code/config end to end; not executed (for the Angular app, because the npm registry was unreachable from the analysis sandbox).
confidence.needs-host-check: Depends on the production server or deploy procedure, which is not in the repository. Check on the host before acting.

effort.L: more than three days or cross-cutting

decisions.question: How far to shrink the git repository?
options: (a) Re-point tags 0.1-0.8 to their twins on main and force-push tags: clone ~9.3 GB -> ~1.8 GB, no rewrite of main.
(b) Additionally purge assets/ from main history with git-filter-repo: clone -> tens of MB, every commit hash changes.
(c) Leave as is; agents use partial clones.
decisions.recommendation: (a) now, (b) when there is a quiet window; tell anyone with a clone to re-clone after (b).
decisions.reversible: (a) yes (the old targets are plain commits behind lightweight tags and can be re-pushed from any full clone that still has them); (b) only from a backup mirror.

decisions.question: What does 'deleted' mean for readers?
options: Hidden everywhere (public and admin), no restore.
Hidden on the public site; admin lists hide by default with an ADMIN-only 'show deleted' toggle and a restore action.
Switch children to hard deletes (inserts are already audited; the delete path must write its own DELETE audit rows) and keep soft delete only for top-level entities.
decisions.recommendation: Option 2, combined with option 3 for child rows (ANL-26).

decisions.question: What may an EDITOR do?
options: Keep today's model (content + translations + all file operations).

EDITOR keeps content and plain-text translations; HTML translations, file-structure changes (category moves, renames, reconcile, cleanup, empty trash, forget missing) and language deletion become ADMIN-only.
decisions.recommendation: Option 2. This changes the written rule rather than applying it: php/api/meddleware/auth.php:128-154 counts uploaded files as content (ADMIN or EDITOR), so adopting option 2 means amending that comment and adding a role group for asset structure and HTML translations.

decisions.question: How is the first admin created on a fresh database?
options: Random one-time password printed once by migration.php (email_confirmed = TRUE, force_password_change = TRUE).
Credentials from environment/CLI flags (`php migration.php --admin-email=... --admin-password=...`).
Keep the fixed documented password (not recommended).
decisions.recommendation: Option 1 as the default, option 2 for automation; plus server-side enforcement of force_password_change.

decisions.question: What should GitHub Pages publish?
options: Nothing: delete the workflow.
Only docs/ (the generated reports).
decisions.recommendation: Delete it. The reports contain internal detail about the API that does not need a public URL.

decisions.question: Keep php/config/database.local.php tracked for convenience?
options: Keep it tracked (today) and rely on discipline.
Commit database.dev.php with dev defaults; database.local.php becomes untracked and optional.
decisions.recommendation: Option 2. Agents commit whatever is modified.

decisions.question: What is the minimum quality gate in CI?
options: php -l + PHPStan level 2 (baseline the `$app might not be defined` noise) + API smoke suite on PostgreSQL + ng build + lint + unit tests + secret scan.
Build only.
decisions.recommendation: Option 1, introduced in that order: each step is cheap and each catches a class of issue found in this report.

decisions.question: Which package manager and Node policy for angular/?
options: bun (bun.lock is what exists)
npm (what the scripts call)
decisions.recommendation: Pick one, commit its lockfile, delete the other, and declare a Node range (e.g. >=22.15 <23) instead of an exact pin.

decisions.question: What happens to old/ (the legacy Vue site)?
options: Delete it (history keeps it; tag the last commit that has it).
Keep it.
decisions.recommendation: Delete it after tagging. Its assets are gone, so it no longer works anyway.

decisions.question: Are competitive features (leaderboards, shared scores) planned?
options: Yes: results must be validated server-side first.
No: current trust model is acceptable for personal stats.
decisions.recommendation: Decide before building any shared ranking.

findings.title: Soft-deleted content is still served by the content read endpoints (public site and admin)
locations: php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/characters.php:9-52 (list, minimal, single, random: no deleted filter)
php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/weapons.php:7-25 (same pattern in materials.php, foods.php, banners.php, artifacts.php, enemies.php and the child-table endpoints)
php/api/full_resource.php:277-303 (GET /api/{path}/full lists every parent, deleted or not)
php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/characters_full.php:355-404 (GET /api/characters/{id}/full returns a deleted character)
php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/characters_voice_overs.php:7-45
php/api/full_resource.php:341, php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/characters_full.php:229 (the /full PUT the admin forms use finds the row without checking `deleted`)
angular/src/app (no code under sites/main or shared filters on `deleted`)
findings.what: Deleting is a soft delete (`deleted = TRUE`). The list, single, /minimal, /random and /full parent reads of characters, weapons, materials, foods, banners, artifacts and enemies, and every child-table endpoint, never add `deleted = false`. A few reads do filter (the /api/quizzes and /api/backgrounds lists, /api/quiz/voice-over/random, /api/materials/{id}/usage, /api/dashboard/stats, and the child collections inside /full), so the rule is applied piecemeal. The Angular main site never filters on `deleted` either.
findings.evidence: Local run: `DELETE /api/characters/1` answered 200 'Deleted successfully', after which `GET /api/characters`, `/api/characters/minimal`, `/api/characters/1` and `/api/character/random` all still returned the row with `deleted: true`. Rows stored with `deleted = true` were returned by `/api/weapons`, `/api/weapons/full`, `/api/enemies` and `/api/enemies/full`.
findings.impact: Anything an editor deletes stays on the public site: database pages, quizzes (the public site calls getCharactersMinimal/getCharacters/getWeapons/getMaterials/getFoods/getBannersFull), and random picks. In the admin, deleted rows stay in the lists and still open and save: the forms use PUT /api/<entity>/{id}/full, which does not check `deleted`, so the save succeeds and the row stays deleted (only some per-table PUTs, such as weapons.php:47, answer 404). Children re-inserted on every save (ANL-26) pile up as deleted duplicates in the child-table endpoints.
findings.fix: Settle D2 first. Recommended: public reads return live rows only; admin lists default to live rows, with `?includeDeleted=1` for ADMIN if a restore feature is wanted. Implement it in one place, for example a `DbQuery::live()` helper that adds `_t.deleted = false` when the table has the column, and use it in every GET, in `registerFullResource()` parent queries, and in the characters /full GET (404 for deleted). `DbQuery::count()` (db_query.php:144-151) builds its own SQL without the `_t` alias, so it needs the same filter or paged totals keep counting deleted rows. Add regression tests.
findings.fix_risk: Low to medium. An admin screen may currently rely on seeing deleted rows; there is no restore feature today.
findings.verify: Create, delete, then assert the row is absent from public GET list/detail/full/random, and present only with the ADMIN opt-in.

findings.title: Voice-over audio uploaded through the character form is silently discarded
locations: angular/src/app/sites/admin/characters/character-form/character-form.component.ts:331-347 (appends `vo_audio_{i}_{lang}` file parts)

php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/characters_full.php:62-73 (`_saveAudioFile` -> `_fullSaveUpload` writes php/public/uploads/voice-overs/<name> and sets `audio_<lang>` = '/uploads/voice-overs/...')
php/api/asset_columns.php:364-409 (`resolveAssetBody`: an `audio_<lang>_file_id` already in the payload wins and the new path is dropped; a '/uploads/...' path is not an asset path and is left as is)
php/api/routes/genshin_impact/models/character_voice_over.php:28-31 (model only has `audio_*_file_id`, so `audio_<lang>` is dropped by `fromBody`)
findings.what: Images in the character form go through the new catalogued upload flow, but voice-over audio still rides along as multipart parts handled by the legacy `/uploads` saver. The path it produces is never turned into a `files` row, and the model has nowhere to put a path.
findings.evidence: Local run: POST /api/characters/full with `vo_audio_0_english=About Jean.ogg` answered 201; the file was written to php/public/uploads/voice-overs/About_Jean.ogg; the voice-over row kept `audio_english_file_id = NULL`, and GET /full showed `audio_english: null`.
findings.impact: Editors believe audio was attached and it never is. Orphan files pile up in php/public/uploads, outside the catalogue and the Files page.
findings.fix: In `_applyUploads()`, save voice-over audio with `_saveAssetUpload($file, 'character/voice_overs/<Character>/<type>/<lang>', <free name>, true)`, reusing the naming in `_resolveVoiceOverTarget()`/`_freeVoiceOverName()` and taking the row data from the payload. Set `$vo['audio_<lang>']` to the returned `assets/...` path and `unset($vo['audio_<lang>_file_id'])` so `resolveAssetBody()` catalogues it. Drop the legacy `/uploads` path for audio.
findings.verify: Upload through the form, then check that GET /api/characters/{id}/full shows `audio_english` under assets/character/voice_overs/... and that a `files` row exists.

findings.title: POST /api/auth/login/code/verify acts as an unthrottled 2FA oracle
locations: php/api/routes/users/endpoints/auth.php:923-949 (TOTP checked at :934, before the emailed code at :938; no loginAttemptsExceeded/recordLoginAttempt)
php/api/totp.php:132-148 (±1 step window, no replay tracking)
php/api/routes/users/endpoints/auth.php:703-781 (Google path: TOTP failures are not recorded as attempts either)
findings.what: Without the emailed code, a caller can send any code plus a TOTP guess for a 2FA account. A wrong TOTP answers 403 `totp_invalid`; a correct one answers 400 `invalid_code`. Nothing throttles the endpoint.
findings.evidence: Local run: wrong TOTP -> 403 totp_invalid; current TOTP -> 400 invalid_code; 60 rapid guesses -> all 403, never 429 (POST /api/auth/login returned 429 after 10 failures).
findings.impact: Preconditions: the attacker already has the password, which is exactly the case 2FA exists for, and can send a large number of requests. The oracle finds a currently valid TOTP within roughly 10^5 to 10^6 requests, and that code is then usable on /api/auth/login inside its window. 2FA is reduced to a rate-limit problem.
findings.fix: (1) Check the emailed code first and the TOTP only after it passes, or evaluate both and return one uniform error. (2) Apply `loginAttemptsExceeded()` and `recordLoginAttempt(..., 'bad_totp'|'bad_code')` on this endpoint and on the Google TOTP branch. (3) Keep a per-account TOTP failure window. (4) Store the last accepted TOTP step per user to block replay.
findings.verify: Regression test: responses for a wrong TOTP and a wrong code are indistinguishable, and a 429 follows after N failures.

findings.title: Fresh installs: the seeded admin cannot sign in, and 'forced password change' is only a UI rule
locations: php/migration.php:57-60, 299-320 (seed inserts admin@localhost / Admin1234! without email_confirmed)
php/migrations/users/001_initial_schema.sql:63 (email_confirmed DEFAULT FALSE)
php/migrations/users/017_account_auth.sql:39 (one-off UPDATE that runs before the seed on a fresh database)
php/api/routes/users/endpoints/auth.php:373-379 (login refuses unconfirmed accounts)
php/api/meddleware/auth.php:23-78 (requireAuth never looks at force_password_change)
php/README.md (publishes the default credentials)
findings.what: On an empty database every migration runs first, so 017's 'confirm everyone' UPDATE finds nobody; the admin is then inserted unconfirmed and login refuses it. Separately, `force_password_change` is enforced only by the Angular UI: the API serves everything to such a session.
findings.evidence: Fresh PostgreSQL 16 + `php migration.php`, then login as admin@localhost / Admin1234! -> 403 email_not_confirmed. After confirming by SQL, a session for an account with force_password_change = TRUE got 200 from GET /api/users and GET /api/backups.
findings.impact: A fresh `users` database cannot be signed into with the documented credentials. With the default `file` mail driver the owner can get in through 'forgot password' (a reset also confirms the address) or 'resend confirmation' and the .eml in php/storage/mail/, but nothing documents this; where the `mail` driver is configured, SQL is the only way in. The obvious 'quick fix' of confirming the seed would ship a publicly documented admin password that the API honours until somebody changes it through the UI.
findings.fix: Seed with `email_confirmed = TRUE` and a random one-time password printed once, or one taken from env/CLI flags. Enforce `force_password_change` in `requireAuth()` by allowing only /api/auth/me, /api/auth/password, /api/auth/password/set and /api/auth/logout. Update php/README.md.
findings.verify: Build a fresh database, sign in with the printed password, and check that everything except the password change answers 403 until it is changed.

findings.title: Password-reset and confirmation links sign in without the second factor
locations: php/api/routes/users/endpoints/auth.php:424-465 (POST /api/auth/password/reset: consumes the token, sets the password, then issues a session at :464 without `authTotpRefusal()`)
php/api/routes/users/endpoints/auth.php:255-279 (POST /api/auth/confirm: the same, session at :278)
php/api/routes/users/endpoints/auth.php:364, 724, 738, 934 (password login, Google and the emailed code all check the second factor first)
findings.what: Every other way in calls `authTotpRefusal()` before `authSession()`. The two email-link endpoints go straight to `authSession()`, so for an account with 2FA the link alone is a full sign-in. The reset path works for every 2FA account that has a password. The confirmation path is reachable only in edge cases (an admin clears `email_confirmed`, or a 48-hour confirmation link is still unused after the address was confirmed another way).
findings.evidence: Local run: an account with TOTP enabled; POST /api/auth/login with the right password and no TOTP -> 403 totp_required. POST /api/auth/password/forgot, then POST /api/auth/password/reset with the token from the mail -> 200 with a session token; GET /api/auth/me with it -> 200 (totp_enabled: true).
findings.impact: Whoever can read the mailbox, or gets hold of a reset link (valid 60 minutes), takes over a 2FA account without the second factor, and the reset also signs the owner out and removes their trusted devices. For an ADMIN with 2FA, a mailbox compromise alone gives full admin (backups, restore, accounts). The code states the intended rule itself on the Google path: 'an account with 2FA on must not gain a new way in on the strength of a Google token alone'.
findings.fix: In both handlers call `authTotpRefusal($response, $pdo, $user, $body['totp'] ?? null, $body['device_token'] ?? null)` before `authSession()`. On refusal keep the new password (or the confirmation) but return no session, so the user signs in normally with the second factor. The SPA's reset and confirm pages need the same 2FA prompt the login page has. Accounts without 2FA keep today's behaviour.
findings.fix_risk: Low. The reset and confirm pages must handle `totp_required`.
findings.verify: Replay the local run: for a 2FA account /password/reset answers 403 totp_required with no session, the new password then works together with a TOTP, and a valid TOTP in the reset body gives 200.

findings.title: Google sign-in adopts an account someone else pre-registered with the same address, and keeps their password
locations: php/api/routes/users/endpoints/auth.php:181-249 (anyone can register any address; the account stays unconfirmed with the registrant's password, and nothing prunes it)
php/api/routes/users/endpoints/auth.php:171-176 (`authFindByEmail()` ignores `email_confirmed`)
php/api/routes/users/endpoints/auth.php:735-754 (Google branch: attaches the identity, sets `email_confirmed = TRUE`, signs in)
php/api/routes/users/endpoints/auth.php:107-110, 373-379 (the registrant's password stays valid; the unconfirmed address was the only thing stopping it)
findings.what: Registration creates an unconfirmed account for any address, with a password the registrant chooses. When the real owner of that address later signs in with Google for the first time, the Google branch finds the unconfirmed account by address, attaches the Google identity, marks the address confirmed and signs the owner in. The registrant's password is kept and now works.
findings.evidence: Local run with only Google's signature check stubbed: registered victim@gmail.com with an attacker's password -> password login 403 email_not_confirmed; Google sign-in with a verified claim for that address -> 200; the attacker's password login -> 200, and /api/auth/me shows the same account for both sessions. Production has `google_login_enabled: true` and `login_enabled: true` (https://anotoki.eu/api/settings/public).
findings.impact: Anyone can pre-register the addresses of people likely to join (Gmail addresses, for example) and wait. Once the owner arrives through Google and uses the account, the registrant signs in with the password and can read and change everything in it; the owner sees nothing unusual. A lesser variant needs the owner's click: they open the unsolicited confirmation mail and end up in an account whose password someone else knows.
findings.fix: When the Google branch matches an account that is not `email_confirmed`, clear its password (`password = NULL`) and revoke its sessions and one-time tokens before attaching, or refuse to link and ask the user to confirm the address first. Delete unconfirmed accounts once the 48-hour confirmation window has passed. Normalise the address (ANL-09) before matching.
findings.verify: Pre-register an address, then sign in with Google for it: the registrant's password no longer works (or linking is refused).

findings.title: Sign-in-code endpoints are unthrottled (unbounded mail to confirmed accounts, code guessing)
locations: php/api/routes/users/endpoints/auth.php:896-913 (POST /api/auth/login/code: no limiter)
php/api/routes/users/endpoints/auth.php:923-949 (verify: no limiter)
php/api/one_time_token.php:143-206 (cap of 5 live codes; 5 wrong guesses burn them, which frees the cap)
findings.what: Requesting a code is capped only by 5 outstanding codes per account (10-minute lifetime). For accounts without 2FA, failed verifies burn the codes, so the cap resets on demand. For 2FA accounts a verify without a valid TOTP stops at the TOTP check (auth.php:934) before any code is looked at, so they stay capped at 5 codes per 10 minutes. Neither endpoint uses the login limiter that register, resend, forgot and login use.
findings.evidence: Local run: 30 requests -> 30x 200 and 5 mails; 4 cycles of (5 requests + 5 wrong verifies) -> 20 mails, no 429.
findings.impact: Anyone can make the server send unlimited sign-in-code mails to any confirmed account without 2FA, and about 720 a day to one with 2FA. That means harassment, an exhausted hosting mail quota, and damage to domain reputation that blocks real confirmation and reset mail. For accounts without 2FA, guessing a code costs about 25-in-a-million per 10 requests, with no per-IP cost.
findings.fix: Use the same limiter as /login on both endpoints (per email+IP and per IP), add a per-account issuance ceiling per hour and per day, and record failed verifies as failed login attempts.
findings.verify: Tests: the 11th request in 15 minutes gets 429, and the mail count stays bounded.

findings.title: Admin HTML editor renders stored markup unsanitized (an editor can steal an admin session)
locations: angular/src/app/shared/local-lib/components/html-editor/html-editor.component.ts:400-405 (`el.innerHTML = value`)
angular/src/app/shared/local-lib/helper.class.ts:311-320 (`normalizeHtml` parses with a live-document element)
angular/src/app/sites/admin/localization/translations/html-translation-modal/html-translation-modal.component.html:25-32 (raw translation value into the editor)
php/api/routes/users/endpoints/translations.php:165-237 (EDITOR may write any translation)
angular/src/app/shared/local-lib/services/security.service.ts:336, 343 (JWT and trusted-device token in localStorage)
findings.what: The public renderer (`app-rich-text`) sanitizes with a good allowlist, but the admin editor assigns the raw stored value to a contenteditable element in the live document. `normalizeHtml()` does the same on every keystroke through a `document.createElement('div')`, and images with event handlers run even on detached elements.
findings.evidence: Code path read end to end: html-translation-modal -> app-html-editor [(value)] -> afterValueChange -> el.innerHTML. Not executed in a browser here, because the frontend could not be built in the sandbox.
findings.impact: Anyone who can write translations (EDITOR, an import file, a restored backup, SQL) can run script in an ADMIN's browser when the admin opens that key. The script can read the admin JWT and trusted-device token from localStorage, which gives full admin: backups, accounts, sessions.
findings.fix: Pass the value through `sanitizeRichHtml()` before assigning innerHTML in `afterValueChange()` and when leaving source mode. Make `normalizeHtml()` parse with `DOMParser` or `document.implementation.createHTMLDocument()`. Add a CSP for the SPA (ANL-35).
findings.fix_risk: Low. The editor already shows sanitized output in its preview.
findings.verify: Component test: a value containing an image with an event-handler attribute leaves no handler attribute in the editor DOM.

findings.title: Route gate (page locks on API paths) is bypassed by percent-encoding
locations: php/api/meddleware/route_gate.php:41 (compares the raw, still-encoded path)
php/api/site_routes.php:184-210 (prefix match)
php/vendor/slim/slim/Slim/Routing/RouteResolver.php:42 (Slim routes on rawurldecode()d path)
findings.what: The gate matches claimed prefixes against `getUri()->getPath()`, which is still percent-encoded, while Slim decodes the path before routing.
findings.evidence: With /quizzes blocked and /api/quizzes claimed: GET /api/quizzes -> 423, while GET /api/%71uizzes and /api/quizze%73 -> 200 with the data. Maintenance mode is not affected: it is an allowlist, and encoded paths stayed at 503.
findings.impact: 'Naming a path is what turns the sign into a lock' (php/README.md:157) does not hold. Any locked endpoint can be read by encoding one character.
findings.fix: Normalise once, `rawurldecode($request->getUri()->getPath())`, and reject paths that decode to '/..' or contain NUL, in routeGate() (and in maintenanceGate() for consistency). The alternative is to run the gate as route middleware and match on the route pattern.
findings.verify: Test that the encoded variants also get 423.

findings.title: Soft deletes never reach the audit log
locations: php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/characters.php:98-107, weapons.php:64-70 (two of the 37 DELETE handlers that call `DbQuery::update($pdo, $table, ['deleted' => true], $id)`)
php/api/db_query.php:260-279 (audit row written only when `updated_by` is present; its DELETE detection is therefore dead code)
findings.what: No delete handler passes `updated_by`, so `DbQuery::update()` skips the audit write. Three tables with a `deleted` column have no `updated_by` column at all (users, quizzes, file_categories).
findings.evidence: Local run: after DELETE /api/characters/1, audit_logs still held only the two INSERT rows.
findings.impact: The audit screen cannot say who deleted what, which is the question an audit log most often has to answer.
findings.fix: Add a `DbQuery::softDelete($pdo, $table, $id, $userId)` helper that writes the DELETE audit row itself and sets `updated_by` only where the column exists. Passing `updated_by` to `DbQuery::update()` on users, quizzes or file_categories would fail with SQLSTATE 42703 after the audit row is already written (db_query.php:262-278). Use the helper in every delete handler and add a CI grep for `'deleted' => true` outside it.
findings.verify: Delete a row and assert an audit row with action DELETE and changed_by set.

findings.title: Email addresses are case-sensitive (duplicate accounts, failed logins, missed Google linking)
locations: php/api/routes/users/endpoints/auth.php:181-250 (register trims, never lowercases)
php/api/routes/users/endpoints/auth.php:171-176 (authFindByEmail: exact match)
php/api/routes/users/endpoints/auth.php:720, 735 (Google path lowercases before matching)
php/api/routes/users/endpoints/users.php:303-358 (admin create: same)
php/migrations/users/001_initial_schema.sql:62 (UNIQUE on the raw string)
findings.what: Addresses are stored, compared and limited exactly as typed.
findings.evidence: Local run: registered 'Probe.User@Example.com'; login with the lowercase form -> 401; registering the lowercase form -> 201, a second account.
findings.impact: Users locked out by capitalisation; duplicate accounts; Google sign-in fails to attach to a mixed-case registration and creates a second account; the per email+IP limiter can be sidestepped by varying case (the per-IP limit still applies).
findings.fix: Normalise with `strtolower(trim())` on every write and lookup. Add a migration with a unique index on lower(email), after checking production for existing case-duplicates (`SELECT lower(email), count(*) FROM users GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) > 1`).
findings.fix_risk: Medium: needs a production data check before the index.
findings.verify: Login and register tests with case variants.

findings.title: Repository weighs 9.3 GB: 7.5 GB is reachable only through orphaned tags 0.1-0.8
locations: refs/tags/0.1 ... 0.8 (point at a pre-rewrite lineage that is not on main; 165 commits reachable only through them)
main history: 1.78 GB of deleted `assets/` blobs (untracked 2026-09-04, commit 29e7f4aba)
findings.what: A full clone downloads 9.27 GB of packed blobs (8.7 GB .git on disk) for a 47 MB checkout. Tags 0.1-0.8 keep an old, rewritten history alive, and each has a same-message, same-date twin on main: 0.1->52ae7f8c1, 0.2->086edd140, 0.3->0eda76724, 0.4->8dddeafab, 0.5->c28fcf0cb, 0.6->8d816bda3, 0.7->0991c5a80, 0.8->768e81010.
findings.evidence: `git rev-list --objects` accounting: all blobs 9.27 GB; reachable from main 1.79 GB (1.78 GB of it assets/); only via tags or other refs 7.48 GB. None of the tag commits 0.1-0.8 is an ancestor of main.
findings.impact: Every full clone (agents, new machines) pulls about 9 GB (about 3 minutes here; the default shallow CI checkout is unaffected), which risks GitHub size limits. Tags that are not on main mislead `git describe`, changelog tooling and 'diff since release'.
findings.fix: Settle D1. Step (a), cheap and non-rewriting: re-point the eight tags to their main twins and force-push the tags; fresh clones drop to about 1.8 GB. Step (b), optional and destructive: purge `assets/` from main history with git-filter-repo, then re-tag and force-push, which gives clones of tens of MB. Until then, agents should clone with `--filter=blob:none` or `--depth 1`.
findings.fix_risk: (a) low, but changes tag hashes seen by anyone who fetched them. (b) high coordination: every hash changes.
findings.verify: A fresh `git clone` measures the size; `git tag --no-merged main` prints nothing (today it prints 0.1-0.8).

findings.title: GitHub Pages workflow publishes the whole repository; its site is broken
locations: .github/workflows/static.yml:36-40 (`path: '.'`, runs on every push to main; 43 runs so far)
findings.what: Every push to main uploads the entire repository as a static site, including php/, docs/ and the tracked dev database config. The root has no index.html since the legacy app moved to old/. docs/security/findings.json on that site carries the old JWT fallback verbatim (ANL-12).
findings.evidence: https://irelevant25.github.io/anotoki-genshin-impact/ -> 404; /README.md and /docs/security/findings.json are served; /old/ serves the legacy shell, whose assets are no longer in git.
findings.impact: A confusing second, broken 'site'; source and config republished outside GitHub's UI; wasted CI minutes.
findings.fix: Delete the workflow and unpublish Pages in the repo settings, or publish only a built docs/ folder.
findings.verify: The Pages URL answers 404 or disabled; the Actions tab shows no Pages runs.

findings.title: Credential config files are tracked or unprotected in git, and the old JWT fallback secret is public
locations: .gitignore:23-33 (ignores only google.php, database.local.php and jwt.local.php; the first two are tracked anyway, database.local.php deliberately, per the comment)
php/config/google.php (comment says 'committed rather than local', contradicting .gitignore:27)

php/config/site.local.php, mail.local.php, backup.local.php, google.local.php, cors.local.php (read by config/site.php:24, api/mail.php:49, config/backup.php:29, api/google_identity.php:45 and api/helpers.php:20, and not ignored by git; config/site.php:16 and config/mail.php:12 wrongly say they are)
commits 8ae6b7167 / 44e482a15 (untracked, then re-added the same day)

php/config/jwt.php, docs/security/findings.json, docs/security/security-report-2026-09-05-17-49.html (a 55-character former fallback secret: in jwt.php history up to 7756ccd13, and verbatim in the current tree in the SEC-01 evidence of both docs)
findings.what: .gitignore does not protect tracked files, and most `*.local.php` overrides the code reads are not ignored at all. database.local.php currently holds only local-dev values (postgres on 127.0.0.1, 4-character password), but it is the file the README tells you to fill with real credentials.
findings.evidence: `git ls-files php/config` lists both files, and `git check-ignore` matches none of the other overrides except jwt.local.php. A redacted scan of every historical version shows only local host/user values. gitleaks 8.24.2 (default rules) found nothing in history or tree; its rules do not catch a custom constant such as the old JWT fallback. GitHub Pages serves docs/security/findings.json publicly (ANL-11).
findings.impact: Once anybody puts real values into database.local.php, or creates mail.local.php, backup.local.php, google.local.php, cors.local.php or site.local.php, `git commit -a` or `git add -A` (typical agent behaviour) publishes them. The old JWT fallback must be treated as known to everyone. Every token must also name a live, random 128-bit session id (session.php:84), so the old key alone does not let anyone forge a working token today; it still must not be the production secret (SEC-01 says the environment was re-keyed; confirm it for production).
findings.fix: Add `php/config/*.local.php` to .gitignore. Commit `database.dev.php` with dev defaults and make every loader fall back local -> dev -> template: config/db.php:34 and config/backup.php:124 already fall back to the template, but php/migration.php:337 and endpoints/migrations.php:13 require database.local.php outright and would crash on a fresh clone. Then run `git rm --cached php/config/database.local.php`, settle the google.php/.gitignore contradiction and fix the two 'gitignored' comments. Add gitleaks with a custom rule for `*.local.php` and `'password' =>` to a pre-commit hook and CI. Confirm the production JWT secret differs from the published fallback.
findings.fix_risk: Low. Developers need to create their local file once.
findings.verify: `git ls-files '*.local.php'` is empty; `git check-ignore php/config/mail.local.php` matches; CI secret scan passes.

findings.title: Frontend toolchain is fragile: `npm start` needs nvm and an exact Node, lint cannot run, no tests
locations: angular/start.js:26-32, 73-78 (`execSync('nvm use ...')` whenever Node is not exactly 22.15.0; exits 1 when it fails, before the client is regenerated)
angular/package.json:5-7 (engines: node exactly 22.15.0)
angular/eslint.config.js:3-5 (imports @angular-eslint/* which are in neither devDependencies nor bun.lock); :20 (ignores src/app/generated/, but the generated client lives in src/app/api/)
angular/README.md (describes Karma tests that do not exist; there are 0 *.spec.ts files and no PHP tests)
angular/bun.lock (the only lockfile, while the scripts call npm/npx; lite-server only backs the `server` script at package.json:22, which no documented workflow uses)
findings.what: The documented entry points depend on the author's Windows setup (nvm-windows), and quality tooling is not runnable as committed.
findings.evidence: Static review of package.json, start.js, eslint.config.js and bun.lock. Execution was not possible here because the npm registry is blocked in the analysis sandbox.
findings.impact: On Linux or macOS (cloud agents, CI) `npm start` exits unless Node is exactly 22.15.0, because nvm is a shell function there and `execSync('nvm use')` fails. `npm run lint` fails on missing modules. Agents have no automated regression net.
findings.fix: Replace the nvm switch with a version-range check (or `.nvmrc`) and keep the client regeneration. Add @angular-eslint/* matching Angular 21 and fix the ignore path. Choose one package manager and commit its lockfile. Add unit tests (Angular 21's `@angular/build:unit-test` builder runs Vitest) plus a PHP API smoke suite (Appendix C). Remove lite-server and its `server` script.
findings.verify: CI runs `ng build`, lint and tests on Linux.

findings.title: Generated API spec and client are not reproducible across machines
locations: angular/generate-api.mjs:278, 398 (`localeCompare` with no locale)
angular/generate-api.mjs:290, 301, 443, 454, 468 (writes CRLF explicitly)
php/generate-api-spec.php (route `file` stored as an absolute path, e.g. 'F:\Repositories\...')
.gitattributes (absent from the repository)
findings.what: Output depends on the OS locale, the OS line endings and the checkout path.
findings.evidence: Regenerated on Linux: the spec content was identical apart from 399 absolute paths; the client was identical apart from CRLF and method order in 3 services (auth, banner, lookup). Slovak collation sorts 'ch' after 'h', so createBannerCharacter and createBannerFull swap.
findings.impact: Any agent running `npm run api` (or `npm start` on exactly Node 22.15.0) on Linux produces large no-op diffs, which buries real changes and invites accidental commits.
findings.fix: Use `a.localeCompare(b, 'en')` or a plain code-point compare; write LF; store paths relative to the repo root; add `.gitattributes` (`* text=auto eol=lf`, binaries marked).
findings.verify: Regenerating on Windows and on Linux gives byte-identical output.

findings.title: Production sits behind Cloudflare, but every rate limit and stored IP uses REMOTE_ADDR
locations: php/api/session.php:46-61 (`requestIp()`: REMOTE_ADDR only; its comment says a proxy would make the limit shared and names the fix, a trusted-proxy list)
php/api/session.php:175-188 (10 failures per email+IP and 50 per IP per 15 minutes)
php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/feedback.php:42-51, 85-92 (feedback limit keyed on a hash of REMOTE_ADDR)
user_sessions.ip, user_login_attempts.ip, user_trusted_devices.ip, feedback.ip (the stored addresses, ANL-28)
findings.what: anotoki.eu, www.anotoki.eu and umami.anotoki.eu resolve to Cloudflare addresses (104.21.25.199, 172.67.134.133, 2606:4700:3036::ac43:8685, 2606:4700:3037::6815:19c7). Unless the origin restores the visitor's address (mod_remoteip with Cloudflare's ranges, or an equivalent the host provides), REMOTE_ADDR is a Cloudflare edge address, and the code trusts nothing else.
findings.evidence: DNS lookups from the analysis sandbox; code review. The origin's web-server configuration is not in the repository.
findings.impact: If REMOTE_ADDR is Cloudflare's, the per-IP ceiling (50 failures per 15 minutes) is shared by everyone who comes through the same edge address, so one person failing logins can lock unrelated users out of login, registration and password reset. An attacker whose requests arrive from several edge addresses gets 10 guesses per account per address instead of 10 in total. The fixes for ANL-03 and ANL-04 inherit both problems, and stored addresses are useless for investigation.
findings.fix: Check first, in production: `SELECT ip, count(*) FROM user_login_attempts GROUP BY ip ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 20`. If the top addresses are Cloudflare's, enable mod_remoteip at the host (`RemoteIPHeader CF-Connecting-IP` plus `RemoteIPTrustedProxy` for Cloudflare's published ranges), or implement the trusted-proxy list the comment in session.php describes: take CF-Connecting-IP only when REMOTE_ADDR is inside Cloudflare's ranges. Consider Cloudflare rate-limiting rules for /api/auth/* as a second layer.
findings.fix_risk: Low, as long as the header is trusted only from Cloudflare's ranges.
findings.verify: New rows in user_login_attempts show visitor addresses, not Cloudflare ranges.

findings.title: Asset-library operations can silently break the live site, and editors are allowed to run them
locations: php/api/asset_catalogue.php:435-527 (Reconcile moves every file in a folder no category claims into assets/unfiled)

php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/file_categories.php:211-267 (changing a category path moves all its files in one request, without batching or raising PHP's time limit; the disk renames run inside a DB transaction that cannot undo them)
php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/file_categories.php:104-137 (`_categoryMoveOneFile` flattens every name to its basename; collisions get an md5 suffix)
php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/file_categories.php:269-305 (deleting a category moves every file into unfiled, flattened the same way)
php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/file_categories.php:318-397 (rename); files.php:549-604 (forget missing), 610-646 (empty trash: permanent)
php/api/meddleware/auth.php:128-154 (the written rule counts uploaded files as content, ADMIN or EDITOR; these routes follow it, so restricting them is the policy change D3 asks about)
findings.what: Structural and destructive file operations are editor-level and act immediately on the served tree.
findings.evidence: Code review. The public site resolves much art by folder and name convention (asset_columns.php header; material-icon directive). Older trees had folders such as emoji/, wallpaper/ and wishes/ that no seeded category claims.
findings.impact: Moving, renaming, deleting or reconciling can break art on the public site without any error: files referenced through `*_file_id` follow their rows, but art found by folder and name convention does not. A category path change or delete also flattens every file name to its basename, so the character/voice_overs tree (about 76k files, names four folders deep) would collapse into one folder even when the move completes, and a time-out half-way leaves disk and catalogue out of sync.
findings.fix: Settle D3. Restrict structural and destructive file operations to ADMIN; give Reconcile a dry-run listing of the strays it would move; when only a category's path changes, rename its folder in one operation and keep the file names; queue any per-file moves in batches like convert and cleanup do; confirm every served folder is claimed by a category before reconciling production.
findings.verify: An editor gets 403 on these routes; the reconcile dry run lists the strays; changing a category path keeps nested file names.

findings.title: Large unauthenticated payloads, expensive endpoints, and no general rate limiting
locations: php/api/full_resource.php:146-168, 277-303 (GET /api/{path}/full: every parent with nested children, N+1 queries)
php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/characters_voice_overs.php:13-16 (`pageSize=0` returns every row, for anyone)
docs/performance/runs/20260905T1331Z.json
findings.what: Public list endpoints can return megabytes and cost seconds. Nothing throttles them.
findings.evidence: The project's own benchmark (dev workstation, 52 ms floor): /api/enemies/full 9.65 MB in 1.8 s; /api/weapons/full 2.18 MB in 0.68 s; /api/files/stats 4.95 s; /api/backups/status 2.1 s; /api/files/missing 1.96 s; /api/files/folders 1.77 s (the last four are signed-in only).
findings.impact: On shared hosting, a trivial loop of anonymous requests can saturate PHP workers and the DB.
findings.fix: Paginate or cap public lists (drop `pageSize=0` for anonymous callers); ETag and Cache-Control on public content, as translations already do; fetch children per table with IN(...) instead of per parent; rate-limit at Cloudflare, which already fronts the site (ANL-38), or at the web server.
findings.fix_risk: Low to medium: callers of /full lists expect whole arrays.
findings.verify: The benchmark shows reduced p95 and bytes; a burst of anonymous requests gets 429.

findings.title: `ng build` bundles the whole asset tree, and production config.json is hand-managed
locations: angular/angular.json:49-59 (build assets include ../assets -> output assets/)
angular/public/config.json (dev values: url http://localhost:8000, configuration dev)
findings.what: Every build copies ../assets, about 65-88k files and about 10 GB according to the code's own comments, into dist/. The only committed runtime config is the dev one.
findings.evidence: Repository config. Production https://anotoki.eu/config.json is {"url":"","configuration":"prod"}, so it is maintained on the server.
findings.impact: Slow, huge builds; a naive deploy of dist/ (by a person or an agent) overwrites production config.json with dev values, pointing the live site at localhost.
findings.fix: Keep the ../assets glob only in the development configuration and serve assets from the web server in production. Add a production config (fileReplacements or a deploy step that writes config.json). Document the deploy in the repo.
findings.fix_risk: Medium: check how assets are currently deployed before changing the build.
findings.verify: `ng build --configuration production` output has no assets/ tree and carries the prod config.

findings.title: Production storage/ and vendor/ appear to sit under the web root, protected only by rules outside the repo
locations: php/README.md ('Deploying to Hosting' copies api/, config/ and vendor/ into public_html)
php/config/backup.php:39, php/api/error_log.php:28, php/api/mail.php:122 (storage/ is created beside api/)
findings.what: storage/ holds full pg_dump backups (including password hashes), error logs (IP addresses, user ids, paths), mail files (dev driver), caches and the asset trash.
findings.evidence: https://anotoki.eu/storage/cache/asset-stats.json -> 403 and /vendor/composer/installed.json -> 403, whereas unknown paths such as /php/... get the SPA shell, so something denies these two prefixes. anotoki.eu is proxied by Cloudflare, so the rule may sit at Cloudflare or at the origin, and a 403 does not prove the directories exist; check on the host. /api/openapi.json -> 404. No deny rule is in the repository.
findings.impact: One server-config change or migration to another host and backups or logs become downloadable. Error-log file names are predictable (errors-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl).
findings.fix: Move storage/, config/ and vendor/ outside the document root (make the storage path configurable), or have the code write `storage/.htaccess` with `Require all denied` whenever it creates the directory. Document the real production layout in the repo.
findings.verify: Requests to /storage/** return 403 or 404 from a rule that is in the repository.

findings.title: SPA hardening: no Content-Security-Policy, bearer secrets in localStorage
locations: angular/src/index.html (no CSP meta; umami script from umami.anotoki.eu)
angular/src/app/shared/local-lib/services/security.service.ts:336, 343, 454 (JWT and 30-day trusted-device token in localStorage)
php/api/index.php:349-374 (strict CSP only on API responses)
findings.what: The API sends strict security headers, but the SPA (served by the web server, config not in the repo) has no CSP in the repository. Session and device secrets are readable by any script on the origin, and the main site and admin share it.
findings.evidence: Repository review; production SPA headers could not be read from the sandbox.
findings.impact: Any XSS, for example ANL-06, turns directly into account takeover, including admin.
findings.fix: Serve a CSP for the SPA (`default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://umami.anotoki.eu https://accounts.google.com/gsi/client; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, then adjust for Google Identity Services and inline styles), and commit it as .htaccess or a documented server config. Longer term, consider an HttpOnly cookie session for the admin.
findings.fix_risk: Medium: CSP needs testing with Google sign-in and the analytics script.
findings.verify: securityheaders.com and the browser console show no violations on main and admin pages.

findings.title: Raw PostgreSQL error text reaches anonymous callers; missing length validation
locations: php/api/index.php:231-241 ('Invalid data: ' / 'Conflict: ' . $exception->getMessage())
php/api/routes/users/endpoints/auth.php:191-208 (no username length or charset rules)
findings.what: SQLSTATE 22xxx and 23xxx exceptions are mapped to 400 and 409 with the driver message attached. The project's own review lists this area as cleared ('no ... DSNs reach the client').
findings.evidence: Anonymous POST /api/auth/register with a 150-character username -> 400 {"error":"Invalid data: SQLSTATE[22001]: String data, right truncated: 7 ERROR: value too long for type character varying(100)"}.
findings.impact: Schema details (column types, constraint names, and on 23505 the conflicting key values) leak. Users see unreadable errors.
findings.fix: Return generic messages or field-level validation errors and log the detail server-side. Validate username (length, allowed characters) and email length before inserting.
findings.verify: The same request gets a 422 with a field error and no SQLSTATE in the body.

findings.title: Error handler crashes on any exception under /api/errors
locations: php/api/index.php:249-251 (`return $response;` where $response is undefined)
php/psalm.xml (suppresses UndefinedVariable, which would have flagged it)
findings.what: The default error handler returns an undefined variable for paths starting with /api/errors.
findings.evidence: PATCH /api/errors -> PHP warning 'Undefined variable $response', then fatal TypeError in ErrorMiddleware; bare 500 text/html with no CORS or security headers. PHPStan also reports it (variable.undefined).
findings.impact: The error-log pages fail opaquely exactly when something is wrong, for example a DB outage while reading.
findings.fix: Build the JSON response as for other paths and skip only the logging. Remove the UndefinedVariable suppression from psalm.xml and run PHPStan level 2 in CI.
findings.verify: PATCH /api/errors -> 405 JSON.

findings.title: Angular 21.2.0 and Vite 7.3.1 (lockfile) are behind 2026 security releases
locations: angular/bun.lock (@angular/* 21.2.0; @angular/build 21.2.0 -> vite 7.3.1)
findings.what: The resolved versions predate fixes for CVE-2026-50557 (namespace sanitization bypass, fixed in 21.2.15), CVE-2026-54265 (two-way binding sanitization bypass, fixed in 21.2.17), CVE-2026-54268 (formatDate DoS, fixed in 21.2.17), and the Vite dev-server file-access bypasses CVE-2026-39364 (fixed 7.3.2) and CVE-2026-53571 (Windows, fixed 7.3.5).
findings.evidence: Versions read from bun.lock; advisories from GitHub Advisory Database (see Sources). PHP dependencies slim/slim 4.15.3 and slim/psr7 1.8.0 have no open advisories.
findings.impact: Low exploitability as written: no SSR, no service worker, no Angular i18n, no two-way binding on DOM security properties found; the Vite issues matter only when `ng serve` is exposed with --host (for example for phone testing on a Windows LAN). Worth patching anyway.
findings.fix: Bump to the latest 21.2.x (>= 21.2.17) or to 22.x, regenerate the lockfile, rebuild, and add `npm audit`/`bun audit` plus `composer audit` to CI.
findings.verify: Lockfile shows the patched versions; audit is clean.

findings.title: Uploads .htaccess does not do what its comments (and SEC-02) say
locations: php/public/uploads/.htaccess:1-14
php/api/full_resource.php:36-46 (writes `php_flag engine off` into public/uploads)
docs/security/findings.json (SEC-02 resolution)
findings.what: The only header the file sets is `X-Content-Type-Options` (:12-14); nothing sends Content-Disposition, so non-images are not forced to download as the comment at :9-11 claims. `php_flag` (:5) is a mod_php directive; under PHP-FPM/CGI, Apache answers 500 for the whole directory.
findings.evidence: File contents. Apache behaviour depends on the host and was not testable here.
findings.impact: Either uploads stop being served (FPM hosts) or the documented download protection is missing.
findings.fix: Wrap the PHP directives in `<IfModule mod_php.c>`; add `<FilesMatch>` with `Header set Content-Disposition attachment` for non-image extensions, plus `Options -Indexes`; or retire public/uploads entirely (ANL-27).
findings.verify: On the host: /uploads/<file>.ogg answers 200 with an attachment disposition, and a .php placed there is not executed.

findings.title: An admin setting a user's password leaves that user's sessions and trusted devices alive
locations: php/api/routes/users/endpoints/users.php:447-479 (the comment at :473-474 says tokens are 'signed, not looked up', untrue since sessions were added; the response note at :477 is accurate today and must be rewritten with the fix)
findings.what: Self-service password changes and resets revoke sessions and trusted devices; the admin reset does not.
findings.evidence: Code review: php/api/routes/users/endpoints/auth.php:449-451 and :640-641 revoke; users.php:470-478 does not.
findings.impact: Resetting a compromised account's password from the admin panel does not sign the intruder out.
findings.fix: Call `revokeSessionsFor($pdo, $id, SESSION_REVOKED_PASSWORD)` and `revokeTrustedDevices($pdo, $id)`, and fix the comment and the note.
findings.verify: The target's old token gets 401 after the admin reset.

findings.title: Two parallel upload systems; the legacy one writes files nothing catalogues
locations: php/api/full_resource.php:18-132 (`_fullSaveUpload` -> php/public/uploads, used by /full multipart parts)
php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/upload.php (POST /api/upload -> public/uploads, random names)
php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/uploads.php (new flow -> assets/ + catalogue)
findings.what: Legacy upload paths ('/uploads/...') never become `files` rows, so they cannot be stored in `*_file_id` columns.
findings.evidence: See ANL-02 for the live consequence.
findings.impact: Silent data loss (ANL-02), orphan files, two sets of hardening rules to keep in step (ANL-21).
findings.fix: Route every write through `_saveAssetUpload()` plus the catalogue. Retire /api/upload and the multipart file parts of the /full endpoints once the admin no longer sends them.
findings.verify: grep finds no remaining writer to public/uploads.

findings.title: Personal data (IP addresses) kept without retention; a comment claims the opposite
locations: php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/feedback.php:40 ('The address itself is never stored') vs :118 (stores `ip`)
php/migrations/genshin_impact/011_feedback_origin.sql (feedback.ip, feedback.mac)
user_sessions.ip, user_login_attempts.ip, user_trusted_devices.ip (none pruned; trusted_device.php:44-46 fills the last) and php/api/error_log.php (30-day logs with IP)
findings.what: IP addresses (personal data under GDPR, and the audience is Slovak/EU) accumulate indefinitely in four tables.
findings.evidence: Schema and code review; no DELETE or prune job for these tables exists.
findings.impact: Compliance exposure and a stale comment that misleads maintainers. If the host does not restore visitor addresses behind Cloudflare, the stored values are Cloudflare's and useless as well (ANL-38).
findings.fix: Add retention jobs (for example login attempts > 90 days, feedback IP nulled after N days, ended sessions trimmed), a privacy notice, drop the unused feedback.mac column, and fix the comment.
findings.verify: Scheduled job runs; counts of old rows go to zero.

findings.title: A signed-in user can move their own quiz rows into another account
locations: php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/quiz_states.php:63-82 (PUT: `QuizState::partialToDbArray()` at :74 writes every model field in the body, `user_id` included; the guard added at :82 checks only the path)
php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/quiz_stats_history.php:53-70 (the same pattern; update at :62-65)
php/api/routes/genshin_impact/models/quiz_state.php:6 and models/quiz_stats_history.php:6 (`user_id` is a model field)
php/api/meddleware/auth.php:169-182 (`requireSelfOrAdmin()` looks at the route argument only)
findings.what: Both PUTs check that the path's user_id is the caller, then run `UPDATE ... SET <body fields>`, and the model lets `user_id` through.
findings.evidence: Local run: user 37 created a quiz state, then PUT /api/quiz-states/37/1 with body {"user_id": 38} -> 200; the row now belongs to user 38, with user 37's content.
findings.impact: Any signed-in user can plant quiz state or statistics in anyone else's account, for example to spoil their daily quiz. If the target already has a row with that key, the unique-violation text comes back (ANL-13). It contradicts the project's own 'cleared' IDOR review (see §7).
findings.fix: Remove the key columns from the update (`unset($data['user_id'], $data['quiz_id'], $data['character_id'])`) or pin them to the path values, and check the other PUTs guarded by `requireSelfOrAdmin()` for the same pattern.
findings.verify: The same PUT leaves the row with user 37 (or answers 422).

findings.title: Stale or misleading documentation and comments (agents read these)
locations: docs/security/README.md ('Psalm ... already in composer.json': composer.json has no require-dev)
docs/security/findings.json (SEC-02 claims .htaccess forces downloads; it does not)
php/api/routes/users/endpoints/users.php:473-474 (tokens 'signed, not looked up')
php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/feedback.php:40 ('address never stored')
angular/README.md (Angular CLI 19.2.10, Karma; actual Angular 21.2, no tests)
php/README.md (a 'PHP CRUD API Template' with 'Swagger annotations' and 'openapi-generator-cli'; empty 'Flyway' header; generic deploy steps; default admin that cannot log in, ANL-05)
php/generate-api-spec.php:24-31 (says row shapes come from schema files; it replays migrations since :483)

angular/src/app/sites/main/features/quizzes/shared/daily.ts:23-25 ('clearing the browser cannot reroll'; true for which quizzes, not for the question: character-quiz.class.ts:158-165 uses Math.random)
php/api/helpers.php:28-31 (CORS default anotoki.eu) vs php/config/mail.php and google.php examples (anotoki.sk, which does not resolve)
README.md (a 'Next version 1.0' TODO list, not a README)

php/api/openapi.json (stale: 369 operations for 399 routes; 33 current routes missing, 3 obsolete /api/stats/{id} ones present; its description still says '9 registered routes are left out'; last regenerated in cde22f9a2 on 2026-09-03; docs.html serves it)
php/config/site.php:16, php/config/mail.php:12 ('gitignored, like the other .local.php files': they are not, ANL-12)
php/config/database.local.php:5 ('database.local.php is gitignored': it is tracked)
.gitignore:30-31 (the API 'refuses to start' without a JWT secret: it starts, and only signing and verifying tokens fail)
findings.what: The codebase leans heavily on explanatory comments; several now contradict the code.
findings.evidence: Each item checked against the code at commit 17a0c5472.
findings.impact: Agents that trust comments will make wrong decisions (for example assuming uploads are forced to download, that the default admin works, that a new *.local.php file cannot be committed, or that openapi.json describes the API).
findings.fix: Correct the items; regenerate openapi.json (`cd angular && npm run api`) in a commit of its own; add a 'comments must match code' check to review; write a real top-level README (what, stack, setup, deploy).
findings.verify: Re-read each item.

findings.title: optionalAuthUser() accepts revoked (signed-out) tokens
locations: php/api/meddleware/auth.php:112-126
findings.what: Optional-auth endpoints (feedback) verify the signature only, not the session.
findings.evidence: After POST /api/auth/logout, POST /api/feedback with the old token stored the feedback with that account's user_id, username and email.
findings.impact: A leaked old token can still post feedback in someone's name. Minor, but inconsistent with the session model.
findings.fix: Check `findSession()` and the session's user_id as `requireAuth()` does.
findings.verify: After logout, feedback is saved as anonymous.

findings.title: Quiz results are client-asserted and unthrottled; the voice quiz ships the answer with the question
locations: php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/quiz_progress.php:117-169 (win, attempts and difficulty from the body)
php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/user_quiz_history.php:32-46 (inserts history without updating totals)
php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/quiz_voice_over.php:27-69 (returns character_id and name with the clip)
php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/quiz_progress.php:63-93 (state blob stored as-is, no size cap)
findings.what: The server records whatever the browser says happened.
findings.evidence: Code review.
findings.impact: Fine for personal stats. It would block leaderboards or any competitive feature, if one is planned (none is in README.md or the changelog; see D10). Unthrottled writes and uncapped state allow database bloat.
findings.fix: Before any competitive feature: server-side answer checking with a question token. Now: rate limits, a cap on state size (for example 64 KB), and retiring POST /api/user-quiz-history.
findings.verify: Tests for size cap and throttle.

findings.title: Child rows are soft-deleted and re-inserted on every save (unstable ids, growth, asymmetric shapes)
locations: php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/characters_full.php:252-334
php/api/full_resource.php:335-370

php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/characters_full.php:393-403 (GET returns `talent_cost` and flat `ascension_cost`; POST at :160-189 and PUT at :276-298, :316-324 expect `talent_costs` and nested `ascensions[].costs`)
findings.what: Each save gives every child a new id and leaves the old copy as a deleted row.
findings.evidence: Code review; the voice quiz stores `voiceOverId` in saved state (quizzes/voice/voice.component.ts:73).
findings.impact: Unbounded table growth; stale references (saved quiz state, audit record ids); deleted duplicates in the child-table endpoints (ANL-01); the asymmetric characters /full shape is a trap for client code.
findings.fix: Upsert children by id (diff) or hard-delete them (write DELETE audit rows on the way; inserts are already audited). Align the characters /full GET and PUT shapes and regenerate the client.
findings.verify: Saving twice keeps child ids stable.

findings.title: HTTP interceptor sends the JWT to any destination; dead cache code from another project
locations: angular/src/app/shared/local-lib/services/http.interceptor.ts:17-32 (cache for '/enums/' and '/hodnotaCiselnika/' that never matches this API)
angular/src/app/shared/local-lib/services/http.interceptor.ts:50-57 (Authorization added regardless of host)
findings.what: A latent leak: the first HttpClient call to a third-party URL would carry the session token.
findings.evidence: No such external call exists today (only the GIS script tag).
findings.impact: None today; easy to trip later.
findings.fix: Attach the token only when the URL is under the configured backend or '/api/'; delete the dead cache block.
findings.verify: Unit test on the interceptor.

findings.title: `sanitize` input on AbstractInputComponent actually disables sanitization
locations: angular/src/app/shared/local-lib/abstract-input.class.ts:38, 61-67
findings.what: `sanitize = true` calls `bypassSecurityTrustHtml()`. Nothing sets it today.
findings.evidence: grep: no usages.
findings.impact: A footgun for the next person, or agent, who reads the name.
findings.fix: Rename it to `trustHtml` or remove it.
findings.verify: grep shows no bypass reachable from inputs.

findings.title: Main-site features are not split per route
locations: angular/src/app/sites/main/main.routes.ts:1-29 (every feature imported statically)
angular/src/app/app.routes.ts:8-11 (the whole main site is one lazy `loadChildren` chunk)
findings.what: Each site is one lazy chunk. Within the main site nothing is split, so the first visit to any public page downloads quizzes, games, database pages and profile together.
findings.evidence: Code review; bundle size not measured (no build possible here).
findings.impact: Slower first public page. The chunk is lazy, so the 500 kB initial budget does not measure it and will not catch its growth.
findings.fix: Use `loadComponent` or `loadChildren` per feature.
findings.verify: The `ng build` stats show a lazy chunk per feature.

findings.title: Audit writes swallow PDO errors inside transactions (PostgreSQL then aborts the transaction)
locations: php/api/db_query.php:321-342 (`catch (\PDOException) {}` in writeAuditLog)
findings.what: In PostgreSQL a failed statement aborts the surrounding transaction. Catching the error hides the cause, and the next statement fails with 'current transaction is aborted'.
findings.evidence: Code review; /full saves run inside transactions.
findings.impact: Rare (only if audit_logs is broken), but it turns into a misleading error far from its cause.
findings.fix: Use a SAVEPOINT around the audit insert, or let the error propagate now that the table always exists.
findings.verify: Test with audit_logs renamed: the error names the audit insert.

findings.title: Asset file names keep inner dots, so double extensions such as `x.php.png` can land in the served tree
locations: php/api/asset_naming.php:31-43 (`_assetPathSegment()` strips separators and leading dots, keeps inner dots)
php/api/routes/genshin_impact/endpoints/uploads.php:64-68, 138 and files.php:262-266 (file names come from the client, or a server default)
php/api/full_resource.php:76 (the legacy saver, by contrast, replaces every dot)
findings.what: Names are sanitised per path segment, but a stem such as `shell.php` survives. The extension allowlist and the image check look at the last extension and the bytes, and the original is kept beside its AVIF copy, so `shell.php.png` holding a valid PNG with PHP in a text chunk is accepted.
findings.evidence: Code review. Whether Apache would run such a file depends on how the host maps PHP: `AddHandler` or `AddType` for .php runs any file with .php among its extensions, while a `<FilesMatch "\.php$">` handler does not. assets/ is gitignored, so any rule the host keeps there is not in the repository either.
findings.impact: Code execution on the host from an EDITOR account, but only on hosts that map PHP by extension anywhere in the name and have no script-refusing rule for assets/.
findings.fix: Replace inner dots in stems (as the legacy saver does), or refuse stems whose inner parts end in a script extension. Keep a rule for assets/ that refuses script extensions anywhere in the name in the documented server config.
findings.verify: An upload named `a.php` is stored without the inner dot, or refused; on the host, any path under /assets/ containing `.php` is refused.
